rules.description: Special Leave Petition (Civil) under Article 136 against a civil judgment, decree, determination or order. Cause title or cover says SLP (C), SLP (Civil), or Special Leave Petition (Civil). Not a civil appeal, writ, review, or miscellaneous application.

Special Leave Petition (Criminal) under Article 136 in a criminal proceeding. Cause title or cover says SLP (Crl.), SLP (Criminal), or Special Leave Petition (Criminal). Not a criminal appeal, writ, or review.
Civil Appeal to the Supreme Court of India, including an appeal by High Court certificate or an armed forces tribunal civil appeal. Cause title or cover says Civil Appeal or C.A. Not an SLP (Civil).
Criminal Appeal to the Supreme Court of India. Cause title or cover says Criminal Appeal or Crl.A. Not an SLP (Criminal).
Writ Petition (Civil) under Article 32 of the Constitution for enforcement of fundamental or other civil rights. Cause title or cover says Writ Petition (Civil) or W.P.(C).
Writ Petition (Criminal) under Article 32 involving personal liberty or a criminal matter. Cause title or cover says Writ Petition (Criminal) or W.P.(Crl.).

Transfer Petition (Civil) seeking transfer of a civil case from one High Court or court to another, typically under Article 139A of the Constitution or Section 25 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Cause title or cover says Transfer Petition (Civil) or T.P.(C).

Transfer Petition (Criminal) seeking transfer of a criminal case from one court to another, typically under Section 406 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Cause title or cover says Transfer Petition (Criminal) or T.P.(Crl.).
Review Petition (Civil) under Article 137 seeking review of a Supreme Court civil judgment. Cause title or cover says Review Petition (Civil) or R.P.(C). Not a curative petition.
Review Petition (Criminal) under Article 137 seeking review of a Supreme Court criminal judgment. Cause title or cover says Review Petition (Criminal) or R.P.(Crl.). Not a curative petition.
Original Suit in the Supreme Court under Article 131, typically a dispute between the Union and a State or between States. Cause title or cover says Original Suit or O.S.
Contempt Petition (Civil) for civil contempt of the Supreme Court or of its orders. Cause title or cover says Contempt Petition (Civil) or Cont.P.(C).
Contempt Petition (Criminal) for criminal contempt of the Supreme Court. Cause title or cover says Contempt Petition (Criminal) or Cont.P.(Crl.).
Election Petition in the Supreme Court, including a Presidential or Vice-Presidential election petition. Cause title or cover says Election Petition.

Arbitration Petition in the Supreme Court under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, typically for appointment of an arbitrator or a related arbitration proceeding. Cause title or cover says Arbitration Petition or Arb.P.
Curative Petition (Civil) filed after dismissal of a review petition in a civil matter. Cause title or cover says Curative Petition (Civil). Not a review petition.
Curative Petition (Criminal) filed after dismissal of a review petition in a criminal matter. Cause title or cover says Curative Petition (Criminal). Not a review petition.

Miscellaneous Application (M.A.) or Interlocutory Application (I.A.) in a pending Supreme Court matter, including restoration, clarification, modification, listing, or a similar application. Cause title or cover says M.A., I.A., Miscellaneous Application, or Interlocutory Application. Not a fresh SLP, appeal, writ, review, or curative petition.

If Vakalatnama is not in this pack or prints no AOR, use the Memo of Appearance footer, then the last page of the Main Petition (very end: Drawn By, Filed on, DRAWN & FILED BY, Advocate for Petitioner/Respondent, Chamber lines under the name). relief_sort.description: Main prayer body only from the Main Petition last 2-3 pages. Copy the text under the heading Main Prayer or Prayer. petition_date.description: Date of this petition from the last page of the Main Petition, after the heading Main Prayer or Prayer. Use the date printed next to Date, Date Drafted, or Date Filed on. If both Date Drafted and Date Filed on are printed, use only the Date Drafted date. Return the date as printed, without the label. Do not use a date inside the prayer, an impugned-order date, or a date from any other document. Leave null if none of those labels is printed after the prayer.
petition_date.title: Petition Date

inconsistencies.description: Spelling mismatches between fill and verify sources, plus an ORGANIZATION party with no acting_through. Always include a letter-level mismatch of the Cause Title main petitioner or main respondent versus petitioner 1 / respondent 1 on the Main Petition starting pages (e.g. Shalija vs Shailja). Cover Page has only one name per side; extra parties continue on later starting pages. Also flag when that Cause Title person is missing on those pages, is a different person than petitioner 1 / respondent 1, or is listed on the other side. Extra parties are not a mismatch against Cover Page And Anr/Ors. Also record Impugned Order case number, date, or forum mismatches across Impugned Order, Main Petition, Cover Page, AOR's Certificate, and Affidavit. Also record printed AOR chamber/office address mismatches across Vakalatnama, Memo of Appearance, Main Petition last page, Listing Proforma last page, and AOR's Certificate. Quote both printed strings. Do not invent an address. Ignore extra Ph. on the same chamber line. Party-name items[].raw_text is Cause Title: "Name"; Main Petition: "Name". items[].id is '1', '2', ….

data_schema.title: LegalExtractRecord

categories.name: Advocate's Checklist
categories.description: The independent advocate/AOR filing-compliance checklist for the current Supreme Court filing, irrespective of petition or appeal type. Identify a checklist heading together with numbered compliance questions and YES/NO/N.A. responses concerning this filing, such as limitation, court fees, copies or annexure certification. Accept CHECK LIST, CHECKLIST, CHECK-LIST and clear OCR/spelling variants. Include all continuation questions and the checklist's own compliance declaration, date and AOR signature/details. These closing elements are not separate AOR's Declaration or AOR's Certificate sections. A government, registry or lower-court checklist reproduced inside another document retains that enclosing document's category.

categories.name: Cover Page
categories.description: The outer cover/title sheet of the current Supreme Court paper book or an independently presented volume. It identifies the court, jurisdiction, case/parties and filing advocate, often with PAPER BOOK, COVER PAGE or For Index Please See Inside. Its function is to introduce the bundle, not to present pleadings, a populated form, a document table or a certification. A Supreme Court cause title alone is insufficient: the opening of the Main Petition and the title blocks of affidavits, applications and other forms belong to those documents. A cover of a reproduced lower-court record remains with that record.

categories.name: Record of Proceedings
categories.description: An independently presented Supreme Court hearing/proceedings record for the current case, headed RECORD OF PROCEEDING, RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS or a clear OCR variant. It records hearing dates, appearances, directions or orders; do not require a particular table layout or a one-page length. Keep the complete record and its continuations together. A separately presented hearing record may start another segment of this category. A chronological history prepared by the petitioner is not this category. A proceedings record copied inside an Annexure or other enclosing document stays there, and the presence of ORDER in the record does not make it an Impugned Order.

categories.name: AOR's Declaration
categories.description: An independent declaration by the AOR/advocate about curing or refiling defects in the current Supreme Court filing. Require a declaration heading and a body stating that defects have been cured, changes are confined to defect curing, or the paper books are complete. Accept DECLARATION, DECLEARTION, DECLERATION and comparable OCR/spelling errors when the body confirms this purpose. Include the declaration's date, signature and contact details. Do not use for the main petition's declarations, a sworn Affidavit, the AOR's pleadings-confined Certificate, or a closing declaration within an Advocate's Checklist or Listing Proforma.

categories.name: AOR's Certificate
categories.description: An independent certificate by the AOR for the current Supreme Court filing, identified by CERTIFICATE or a clear OCR/letter-spaced variant and the AOR's certification that the primary pleading is confined to the pleadings/documents before the court or authority whose decision is challenged, or equivalent filing-certification language. Confirm the current case from the title or surrounding outer filing context; do not require a fixed heading position. Include its own filing date and signature. A signature block alone is insufficient. Certificates inside a Checklist, Listing Proforma, Annexure, Appendix or other enclosing document remain there; defect-curing declarations belong to AOR's Declaration.

categories.name: Index
categories.description: An independent contents index of the current Supreme Court paper book or volume: a structured list/table of documents or particulars and their printed page/folio references. Keep the whole continuing table, including unheaded continuation pages and associated entries, in Index. Document names inside rows never start those documents. Distinguish a genuinely separate master or volume index from continuation of the same table. A heading such as FILING INDEX does not override function: a contents table for the paper book is Index; a standalone submission memo identifying papers being filed and the filing advocate/date is Filing Memo. An index inside a reproduced record remains with that enclosing record.

categories.name: Office Report on Limitation
categories.description: The independent Supreme Court Registry limitation report for the current petition, explicitly headed OFFICE REPORT ON LIMITATION, O/R ON LIMITATION or a clear OCR/spelling variant of that title. Its body or form fields concern whether filing/refiling is within time and any delay. Include its continuation and registry certification. Do not use for an application seeking condonation of delay, ordinary discussion of limitation, or a REPORT OF FRESH CASE, OFFICE REPORT OF FRESH CASE or FRESH CASE REPORT merely containing limitation details. A lower-court limitation report inside an exhibit retains the exhibit's category. Do not invent this section when no qualifying report is present.

categories.name: Listing Proforma
categories.description: The independent first-listing information form for the current Supreme Court filing, irrespective of petition or appeal type. Require the form's purpose and prompt/value structure, not an exact spelling: accept PROFORMA, PERFORMA, PRO FORMA, LISTING PROFORMA/PERFORMA, PROFORMA/PERFORMA FOR FIRST LISTING, PROFORMA OF FIRST LISTING, LISTED PROFORMA and clear OCR variants. Corroborating fields include Acts/sections/rules, the challenged court/order/date, judges, nature or classification of the matter, parties, related cases or listing restrictions. A bare PROFORMA heading without this context is insufficient. Keep all continuation fields and the form's closing date, AOR code, advocate details and signature together, even when the final page lacks its heading. Those closing details are not AOR's Certificate. A similar form inside a reproduced record retains its enclosing category.

categories.name: Synopsis
categories.description: The current Supreme Court filing's narrative summary of the dispute, issues and reasons for seeking relief, normally introduced by SYNOPSIS or a clear OCR variant. Keep its narrative continuation pages, quotations of judgments and document references together. End at the next independently established outer section; a separately introduced LIST OF DATES, LIST OF DATES AND EVENTS or LIST OF EVENTS begins List of Dates & Events. Ordinary dates in narrative do not create that boundary. For a combined SYNOPSIS AND LIST OF DATES heading, classify narrative pages here and date/event chronology pages as List of Dates & Events, subject to the shared-page rule. A synopsis within a reproduced lower-court record stays with that record.

categories.name: List of Dates & Events
categories.description: The independent chronological date/event account prepared for the current Supreme Court filing, usually headed LIST OF DATES, LIST OF DATES AND EVENTS, LIST OF DATES & EVENTS, LIST OF EVENTS or a clear OCR variant. Identify a sequence of dates/date ranges linked to events, arranged as a table or chronological entries. Dates can be full or partial; continuation text and continuation pages need not repeat a date or heading. Keep references to annexures and quoted passages within the chronology. A combined SYNOPSIS AND LIST OF DATES heading belongs here when the page is a chronology rather than a narrative summary. Distinguish from narrative Synopsis and court-generated Record of Proceedings. A lower-court chronology inside a reproduced record retains that record's category.

categories.name: Main Petition
categories.description: The primary substantive pleading for the detected current Supreme Court filing: Special Leave Petition, Writ Petition, Civil or Criminal Appeal, Transfer Petition, Review Petition, Curative Petition, Arbitration Petition, Contempt Petition, Original Suit or another supported main proceeding. Identify its own opening/title and party block followed by substantive pleadings such as facts, questions of law, grounds, declarations and prayers. Include its dedicated opening pages and all continuations through its own prayer, integral verification, drafting/filing dates and advocate details. A matching Supreme Court caption alone is insufficient. Do not require one fixed form, populated case number or SLP-specific Form 28 layout when the current filing identity is otherwise established. Separately introduced AOR's Certificate and main supporting Affidavit are separate sections. Incidental I.A.s are Application, not Main Petition. A lower-court petition or other pleading, or an earlier proceeding reproduced inside another document, remains with that enclosing document.

categories.name: Affidavit
categories.description: The independent sworn affidavit verifying or supporting the primary pleading in the current Supreme Court filing, irrespective of petition or appeal type. Identify AFFIDAVIT or a clear OCR/letter-spaced variant together with sworn statements and deponent, verification or oath/notarial attestation features. Use the affidavit's stated purpose and current case context; party names or an affidavit heading alone are insufficient. Keep all sworn statements, verification and attestation pages together. An affidavit expressly verifying an Application stays with that Application, even if separately headed; this category is reserved for the primary pleading's affidavit. Affidavits reproduced inside Annexures or other records stay with those records. An unsworn AOR certificate/declaration is not Affidavit.

categories.name: Annexures
categories.description: Each independent outer supporting exhibit of the current Supreme Court paper book. Establish its boundary from an annexure separator/cover plus exhibit content, or a matching outer Index row/range aligned with surrounding pages. Keep each complete exhibit as one segment, including its cover, translations and reproduced record pages. NEGATIVE RULE: ANNEXURE P-7, ANNEXURE-P/7 or another annexure label, reference, quotation or subheading inside a continuing Synopsis, List of Dates & Events, Main Petition, Application, Index row, Affidavit, order, appendix or reproduced record does not start Annexures. Keep it in the established enclosing document. A prominent heading is insufficient when adjacent pages continue the same narrative, chronology, pleading, table, numbering, quotation or pagination. Internal petitions, indexes, affidavits, orders and local ANNEXURE NO. 1 labels do not create outer sections. POSITIVE BOUNDARY RULE: start Annexures only where the actual outer exhibit opens and another cue corroborates its label: a separate cover, matching Index range, transition to the indexed source, source-specific certification, or consistent outer folio transition. Start a new segment only for a genuinely new exhibit, including adjacent exhibits. Map printed folios to PDF pages first. An Index mention, petition reference, label or TRUE COPY phrase alone is not a boundary. If continuity conflicts with a label, preserve the enclosing document. Preserve the actual series/number without renumbering or imposing a maximum. DIRECTLY CHALLENGED DECISION EXCEPTION: if the Main Petition's challenge/prayer and outer Index identify a decision and the copy matches its court or authority, case number, date and decision type, classify the complete decision as Impugned Order even if an Index row, separator or cover calls it Annexure P-X. The annexure label is metadata, not the primary category. Other background or supporting decisions remain Annexures.

categories.name: Application
categories.description: Each independent application/I.A. made in the current Supreme Court proceeding for incidental or procedural relief, introduced by its application title or I.A. identity and supported by a body requesting that relief. APPLICATION, I.A., INTERLOCUTORY APPLICATION and clear OCR variants are cues; RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH/SHEWETH or PRAYER alone are not. Keep its pleadings, prayer, signature and affidavit expressly supporting that application together. Internal attachments stay within its supported package unless independently established as outer exhibits or other outer documents. Start a new Application segment for each genuinely separate application, including adjacent applications. Do not use for the primary substantive relief sought by the current filing, or for an application reproduced inside an Annexure or another earlier proceeding.

categories.name: Appendix
categories.description: An independent appendix belonging to the current Supreme Court paper book, established by its outer APPENDIX heading/label and surrounding filing context or a corroborated outer Index entry. Accept APPENDIX, APPENDIX-I/II, numbered/lettered variants and clear OCR errors such as APPENDlX. It commonly reproduces constitutional provisions, statutes, rules, regulations, notifications, schedules or other reference material. Legal subject matter alone is insufficient: legal text filed under an outer Annexure remains Annexures. Keep the entire appendix through its supported end. An APPENDIX within a reproduced High Court petition, judgment, application or other record retains that enclosing document's category, even if it has its own title page, pagination or court caption.

categories.name: Memo of Parties
categories.description: An independent party-list document adopted as its own section of the current Supreme Court paper book, headed MEMO OF PARTIES, MEMORANDUM OF PARTIES or a clear variant. Include its party identities, addresses, procedural designations and continuation pages. A separately indexed outer memo may describe the parties BEFORE THE HIGH COURT or another court below; the lower-court reference alone does not exclude it. However, a memo inside a reproduced lower-court record or Annexure is not an independent outer memo. MEMO OF JUDGMENT/JUDGEMENT qualifies only when the actual document functions as this separately presented party list, not as a judgment. A cause title or party block within Main Petition, Application or an order is not enough.

categories.name: Memo of Appearance
categories.description: An independent appearance memo for the current Supreme Court proceeding, headed MEMO OF APPEARANCE, MEMORANDUM OF APPEARANCE or a clear variant such as MEMO OF APPREARANCE, stating that an AOR/advocate or party appears for a named party. Confirm current proceeding identity from its title/body and outer context. It records appearance rather than granting authority to counsel. A lower-court memo or a memo reproduced inside another document retains the enclosing category. When this memo and a Vakalatnama share one physical page, assign that page to Vakalatnama. A separately starting memo on a different page is its own Memo of Appearance segment; adjacency alone does not combine the two.

categories.name: Impugned Order
categories.description: The complete copy of a decision directly challenged in the current SLP, not a reference to or quotation from that decision. Establish the target from the Main Petition's express challenge and prayer, corroborated by the outer Index, then match the copy using the court or authority, case number, decision date and decision type. Strong agreement on these identifiers establishes identity even if one field is absent or affected by OCR; do not guess from a generic judgment heading or from recency alone. The copy may carry a High Court, tribunal or other lower-authority caption; do not require a Supreme Court caption. PRIMARY-CATEGORY PRECEDENCE: once the directly challenged decision is identified, classify its complete decision and page range as Impugned Order even when an Index row, separator, cover or endorsement labels it Annexure P-X. Preserve the annexure label only as contextual metadata; do not classify that challenged decision as Annexures. Include all caption, party, appearance, judgment/order body, continuation, signature and integral certification pages until a supported new outer-document boundary. Separately presented challenged decisions may form separate segments; an explicitly presented continuous composite order-set remains together. Background, relied-upon or earlier orders not directly challenged remain Annexures when filed as exhibits. Quotations in Synopsis, chronology, Main Petition or other pleadings stay in their enclosing document.

categories.name: Vakalatnama
categories.description: The independent instrument appointing counsel/AOR to act for a party in the current Supreme Court proceeding. Identify its appointment/authorization-of-counsel function and a heading such as VAKALATNAMA, VAKALAT NAMA, VAKALTNAMA, V/A or a clear OCR variant; an abbreviation alone is insufficient. Confirm current proceeding identity from the instrument and outer context. Include signatures, counsel acceptance and integral continuations. If Memo of Appearance shares the same physical page, categorize the page as Vakalatnama. A separately starting Memo of Appearance on another page stays separate. A lower-court vakalatnama or one reproduced inside an Annexure or Application retains its enclosing category. Distinguish PoA/BR, which authorizes a representative rather than serving as this counsel-appointment instrument.

categories.name: PoA/BR
categories.description: An independent Power of Attorney or Board Resolution presented to establish a representative's authority to act for a party in the current Supreme Court filing. A Power of Attorney has a principal/grantor empowering a representative; a Board Resolution has corporate meeting/resolution structure, commonly RESOLVED THAT, authorizing a person to institute or conduct proceedings. Match the represented party and purpose to the current filing; a Supreme Court caption is not required on the underlying instrument. Include its integral signatures, schedules and certification. Do not infer this category merely from power to act or an advocate's signature. Distinguish Vakalatnama and Memo of Appearance. An instrument enclosed in an Annexure or another document remains in that enclosing category.

categories.name: Filing Memo
categories.description: An independent submission/filing memo for the current Supreme Court proceeding, identifying the papers being tendered for filing and the filing advocate/AOR, case particulars or filing date. Headings may include FILING MEMO, FILING INDEX or INDEX OF FILING, with clear OCR variants. Determine function, not title alone: a contents table mapping the paper book's documents to printed pages is Index, even if titled FILING INDEX. A filing-memo row within that table stays Index. Include the submission sheet's own continuation list and signature. A lower-court filing memo or one reproduced inside an Annexure, Application or other enclosing record retains that enclosing category.

categories.name: Court Fees
categories.description: An independent court-fee payment, stamp or endorsement sheet belonging to the current Supreme Court filing. Its primary document function must be recording or evidencing court fees, rather than presenting pleadings, counsel authorization or another substantive form. Court-fee stamps, payment endorsements or fee amounts printed on a Vakalatnama, Application, Cover Page or other document do not change that page's category. An Index entry or Checklist response concerning fees is not Court Fees. A lower-court fee sheet reproduced within an exhibit remains part of the exhibit.

categories.name: Custody Certificate
categories.description: An independently presented custody/surrender certificate issued by a jail or prison authority for the accused/convict/petitioner relevant to the current SLP. Identify CUSTODY CERTIFICATE or a clear variant together with official custody, sentence, surrender or release particulars; match the person and underlying criminal case where available. A Supreme Court caption is not required on the issuing authority's certificate. Keep its continuation and issuing-authority certification together. Classify here when it is an independent outer document, not merely custody statements in a bail/suspension Application. A certificate within a supported Annexure or Application package retains that enclosing category.

splitting_strategy.custom_instructions:
OUTPUT CONTRACT: Use the configured category names and physical PDF page numbers, starting at 1. Return only the Split response fields; do not invent category names, numbered filenames or reason/metadata fields. Follow the category descriptions for document identity and boundaries. Distinct documents may share a category: keep separately established outer documents as separate segments, including adjacent segments of the same category. Do not merge separate Memo of Appearance and Vakalatnama segments merely because the UI groups them downstream.

GENERAL RULE -- CONTINUATION PAGES: Keep a document's opening page, body, table, verification and signature continuations together until a supported new outer-document boundary. A missing repeated heading, internal page-number reset, quotation, Prayer, or mention of ANNEXURE-P/1, Affidavit or another document does not itself start a section. Near-blank scanned pages can remain with an established surrounding document when continuity supports this; do not extend a document through a new cover, Index or distinct section.

INDEX AND FOLIOS: The outer paper-book Index is an inventory, not the listed documents themselves. Reconnect labels, particulars and page-range cells separated by OCR only when row layout or continuation evidence supports them. Cross-check Index ranges with actual headings, content and printed folios. Printed numbers are not physical PDF positions: covers, unnumbered sheets, lettered front matter and new volume covers/Indexes can change the offset. Numbers inside reproduced records are not necessarily outer folios. Do not extrapolate one offset across volumes or create a document solely because the Index lists it; the pages may be absent.

NESTING AND CASE IDENTITY: Once an outer Annexure is established, its reproduced petitions, orders, Indexes, Applications, affidavits and representation documents remain inside it despite their headings or court captions, except for the exact decision directly challenged by the current Main Petition. Determine that challenged decision from the petition's challenge/prayer and outer Index, matched to the copy's court or authority, case number, date and decision type. That complete matching decision is Impugned Order even when presented or indexed as Annexure P-X; the annexure label does not override its primary category. Background and supporting decisions remain inside Annexures. A standalone Impugned Order can have the caption of the court/authority under challenge. A standalone Memo of Parties for that challenged proceeding can also have a lower-court caption; use its category description and outer filing context, not a blanket Supreme-Court-caption requirement.

ANNEXURES AND APPLICATIONS: Cross-check outer exhibit labels and Index particulars; local exhibit numbers inside a reproduced record are not new paper-book exhibits. Support any boundary with document evidence; do not infer a missing annexure from a numbering gap. Keep an uncertain continuous run intact rather than cutting at guessed labels. An Application's Prayer, signatures and expressly supporting affidavit remain with that Application. A distinct application needs its own supported start, not just a continuation carrying another heading or number.

FRONT MATTER AND PETITION: Apply the category descriptions to distinguish cover sheets, content Indexes, submission memos, petitions and forms; a title or court caption alone is insufficient. For a combined SYNOPSIS AND LIST OF DATES heading, assign narrative pages to Synopsis and chronological date/event pages as List of Dates & Events, subject to the shared-page rule. Keep a form's continuation fields and its own closing declaration, certificate, date or signature with that form. Use the AOR's Certificate heading and certification function, without a fixed heading-position requirement. An independent main supporting affidavit is separate; an application-supporting affidavit remains with that Application. Distinguish Office Report on Limitation from a fresh-case report by the category description.

SHARED PAGES: Do not split within a physical page or invent a combined category. If Vakalatnama and Memo of Appearance share a page, use Vakalatnama; a following standalone Memo of Appearance keeps its category for downstream grouping. For other genuinely shared pages, use the first substantive document heading, not a running caption or Index-row reference.

UNCERTAINTY: Use content and category descriptions rather than a compulsory document order or fixed page counts. Documents can be missing, out of the usual order or defective: a missing signature, date, attestation or case number is not proof that the document itself is absent. Use surrounding pages to interpret unreadable continuations, but do not guess when evidence conflicts. Leave genuinely unassignable pages uncategorized and include them; never omit them or force every category to appear.
